nativePatchChecks.notes: The v1 sharply isolated lower-left square and hard L-shaped clipping at native (230,1024) have been reduced to nonblocking texture-density remnants. The reconstructed adjacent water cells and principal caustic contours now connect through the old corner without a comparable rectangular large-cell cutoff. A short vertical density remnant near native x230 around y1080 and below remains visible; its portion inside the selected core ends at y1139, while its continuation in the bottom halo is outside the selected core. A faint horizontal density transition near y1024 in the left strip remains, but the main water color and contours remain connected and it no longer defines the old conspicuous pasted rectangle. Full native and exact selected-core lower-left crop reveal no blocking residual square. Top halo contains natural water with no introduced band or unrelated artifact. Keep v2; no mandatory v3 recommended.

The prior conspicuous horizontal arm of the interior L near native y=1024 is absent. A short, localized near-vertical density transition remains near native x=240 below that line. It is visible at 100 percent, but retains the main blue color and caustic continuity and does not form a blocking L-shaped cell cutoff. No mandatory v3 repair is recommended.

The x230-centered strip has continuous oval water cells over its height. A short near-vertical density remnant in its lower portion remains visible near native x=240, with no long clipped cell boundary or closed rectangular patch. This remnant is nonblocking.

Across the y1024-centered strip, the former straight horizontal texture cutoff no longer persists. Oval contours and caustic branches continue across the old defect line. The localized vertical density remnant near native x=240 is nonblocking.

The selected native core lower-left crop no longer contains the former conspicuous horizontal L arm or isolated rectangular cell replacement. The short density edge near native x=240 below y=1024 remains visible and is assessed as nonblocking rather than described as fully erased.
